key_insight: MicroSyn‑X creates realistic synthetic X‑ray datasets of miniature medical devices so deep networks can be trained and transferred to real surgical X‑rays, enabling robust tracking and real‑time robotic navigation without large annotated clinical X‑ray collections.
problem_solved: Alleviates severe data scarcity and domain‑gap for tracking tiny devices in X‑ray images (limited real X‑rays, annotation difficulty, occlusions and low SNR), enabling reliable sim‑to‑real performance for surgical robotics.
method: Physics‑aware synthetic X‑ray generation: render device models inside anatomical contexts with realistic noise, contrast and viewpoint variability.
Domain randomization and sim‑to‑real adaptation: train deep trackers on diverse synthetic data and refine/transfer to real X‑ray sequences.
Closed‑loop integration: use the learned tracker for low‑latency pose estimation and real‑time robotic control for navigation of miniature devices.
impact: Reduces dependence on costly and risky clinical X‑ray annotation, accelerating development of ML-driven interventional tools; provides a practical path for robust, real‑time tracking and control in surgical robotics.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: synthetic X‑ray generation → neural tracker training → sim‑to‑real transfer → robotic navigation loop.
Side‑by‑side images: synthetic vs. real X‑ray frames with tracking overlays to show visual fidelity and transfer success.
Closed‑loop schematic: robot, imaging source, tracker, controller and latency arrows to illustrate real‑time navigation.
Performance chart: tracking accuracy/robustness and navigation success rates comparing MicroSyn‑X to baseline training on limited real data.
paper_title: Synthetic X‑ray‑driven tracking and control of miniature medical devices
paper_authors: Chunxiang Wang, Wenbin Kang, Mengmeng Sun, Hongchuan Zhang, Chong Hong
